identity.title: Mapping Vinyl Cyanide and Other Nitriles in Titan's Atmosphere Using ALMA

question.value: Can C2H3CN be detected at submillimeter frequencies in Titan's atmosphere and spatially mapped, along with other nitriles, to constrain abundances and photochemistry/circulation?

evidence.quote: These new, high-resolution detections have allowed for the first spatial distribution mapping of C$_2$H$_3$CN on Titan.

findings_qualitative.value: C2H3CN, C2H5CN and HC3N concentrated at south pole; CH3CN in north

evidence.quote: C$_2$H$_3$CN is most abundant over the southern (winter) pole, whereas the longer-lived CH$_3$CN is more concentrated in the north.

claims.hypothesis: C2H3CN is detectable in Band 7 and can be mapped
claims.experiment: Imaged archival ALMA Band 7 Titan data
claims.result: Three firm lines detected plus one tentative; map shows 5 sigma southern peak
claims.finding: First spatial map of C2H3CN, south-polar enriched

evidence.quote: Our C$_2$H$_3$CN map (Figure [3](#fig:maps)) shows a flux peak at $5\sigma$ confidence in Titan’s southern hemisphere

claims.hypothesis: Propane is detectable at radio wavelengths
claims.experiment: Modeled two C3H8 lines with NEMESIS
claims.result: Reduced chi2 1.06 vs 1.73 without; lines blended

evidence.quote: we are unable to place firm constraints on the C$_3$H$_8$ abundance or its vertical profile.

claims.hypothesis: Nitrile distribution reflects circulation reversal and differing lifetimes
claims.experiment: Latitudinal flux profiles with Gaussian fits
claims.result: South enhancement for HC3N, C2H3CN, C2H5CN; CH3CN northern
claims.finding: Consistent with circulation reversal and shorter lifetimes of unsaturated species

evidence.quote: The continued northern enrichment of CH$_3$CN despite the change in season supports a relatively longer chemical lifespan than for the other observed species.
